clue.text: In addition, Scot retired to live in English resort

parts.note: in addition means more, as in 'and more besides'

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the Scottish word is read backwards

parts.note: Mac is a familiar term for a Scotsman
to live means to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a Scotsman has also gone into retirement in an English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' signals the reversal of the Scotsman. MORECAMBE is a seaside town on the Lancashire coast in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a traditional seaside holiday town in Lancashire, an example of an English resort.

clue.text: City that's state capital of Colorado and California

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: capital of says take the capital, first, letter of Colorado

explanation.surface: A question about the state capital of two US states, Colorado and California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is a first letter, not a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca is a city in Saudi Arabia, the holiest site of Islam.

clue.text: Find fault with brief analysis

definitions.meaning: to run someone down is to criticise or disparage them
a summary or quick review of the main points

explanation.definitionFit: Run down is a phrasal verb for criticising, and a rundown is a short summary of the facts.

clue.text: Violent act — possibly due to power being seized

definitions.text: Violent act — possibly due to power being seized

indicators.note: being seized means captured inside, so the letter goes within the rearranged letters
possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A violent event happens, perhaps because power has been seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram and 'being seized' the insertion of P. Read whole, the clue also describes what a coup is, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is the sudden, often violent, overthrow of a government to seize power.

clue.text: Sort of angry male making for wicked sorceress

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of furious man turns into an evil witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a phrase meaning 'rather', but 'Sort' is the anagram signal and 'of' is part of the fodder. 'making for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Morgan le Fay is the scheming enchantress of the Arthurian legends, half-sister to King Arthur.

clue.text: Return from Bramley-producing tree?

indicators.note: return means come back, so the letters are read in reverse
from says the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tree produces Bramley apples in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks MLE out of 'Bramley' and 'Return' turns it to ELM. A Bramley is a British cooking apple, which grows on an apple tree, not an elm.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a large deciduous tree.

clue.text: Material printed on flyer with odd type of ink

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal, so a flyer

indicators.note: odd type of says take the odd-numbered letters, the first and third, of the word ink

explanation.surface: Some fabric has been printed with a peculiar sort of ink and bears a picture of a bird or bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd type of' takes the first and third letters of 'ink', giving IK.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a fabric decorated by wax-resist dyeing, so cloth with a printed pattern.

clue.text: Throw away start in game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it in the rubbish
to go is to set off, begin

explanation.surface: Someone discards the opening of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance in which numbers called out are marked off on cards.

clue.text: Style, fashionable one, finally ends

parts.note: to style someone is to name them, and a term is a name
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fashion style, the trendy one, comes to an end at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' is a link word here, not a last-letter indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end points of a line or route, the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Not, say, this widely fashionable sixties band, perhaps?

definitions.text: Not, say, this widely fashionable sixties band, perhaps?

parts.words: Not, say, this widely fashionable sixties band, perhaps?
parts.note: read as a strip of cloth tied in a knot (sounding like not), very broad, and in vogue in the late sixties: a wide necktie

explanation.surface: Asks whether a well-liked sixties pop group was not this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a pop group but is a strip worn round the neck; 'Not, say' sounds like knot; 'widely' means broad.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper tie is a very wide necktie that was in fashion in the late 1960s and 1970s.

clue.text: Crush a nut noisily

indicators.note: noisily says we want a word that sounds like the nut when spoken

parts.note: a conker is the nut of the horse chestnut tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to smash a nut with a loud crack.
explanation.walkthrough: A CONKER is a horse-chestnut seed, threaded on string for a British children's game. 'Crush' looks like a mere verb in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush an enemy is to defeat them completely, a synonym for overcoming them.

clue.text: Catch people using this oft-repeated phrase quietly

parts.note: a mantra is a phrase or slogan repeated again and again
p is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A slogan, murmured softly, is offered as a way of trapping people.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-trap is a device set to seize trespassers, so something used to catch humans.

clue.text: A short film about opening of Oxford bypass

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the film's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: vid is a shortened form of video, a film

indicators.note: opening of says take the first letter of Oxford

explanation.surface: A brief movie about a road that skirts round the first part of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives O, which 'about' puts inside VID.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it and so steer clear of it, a synonym of evade.

clue.text: Goddess, Roman one exhibited in the Prado originally

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the rearranged letters
originally means in an original, novel way, so these letters are freshly arranged

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A painting of a goddess, perhaps a Roman figure, was first shown at the Madrid museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges THEPRADO into APHRODTE, and 'in' puts I between D and T. The Prado is the great art museum in Madrid; 'exhibited' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Animal cases referred to physician

parts.note: a hippo, short for hippopotamus, is an animal
crates are packing cases

explanation.surface: Instances of animal illness have been passed on to a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like medical cases but means packing crates; 'referred to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek physician called the father of medicine.

clue.text: Express paper boy delivered?

indicators.note: express means to put into words, say out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the paper

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper boy brings round the Daily Express.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the name of the Daily Express newspaper, but it is the verb for speaking. The Sun is a British daily tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, so a baby boy who has been born, or delivered.

clue.text: Journalist covered case involving plot by soldiers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the soldiers come alongside
involving means taking in, so the plot sits inside the case

parts.note: a suit is a legal case
a bed is a garden plot
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A reporter wrote up a trial about a conspiracy by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy but is a flower bed. 'covered' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub-editor is a journalist who checks and corrects copy before publication.

clue.text: Engineer I sent to help operator

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A technician says he sent someone to assist a switchboard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephonist works a telephone switchboard and is often called an operator.

clue.text: Cold as well as far from trendy flat

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out, unconscious
and means as well as
out means unfashionable, the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A chilly and unfashionable apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the adjective, as in a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means absolute or downright, and out-and-out means complete or utter.

clue.text: This order's wrong after recovery, soldiers go here

parts.note: after recovering from illness or injury a person is back, returned to normal
soldiers are sent to the front, the fighting line

explanation.surface: After convalescing, troops are sent to the battle line.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK TO FRONT: soldiers back on their feet are sent back to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged back to front has its order reversed, so its sequence is wrong.

clue.text: During action blackguard falls

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the villain goes inside the case

parts.note: a case is a legal action, a lawsuit
a cad is a dishonourable man, a blackguard

explanation.surface: While a lawsuit is going on, a scoundrel takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, especially one of several small falls.

clue.text: One longing to leave husband

indicators.note: to leave means to go away from, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it, so an ache is a longing

explanation.surface: Someone with a yearning to walk out on their spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one in a suit of cards, or a single point scored.

clue.text: Deed covering what's essential to house sale

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the action surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a deed is an act, an action

indicators.note: what's essential to means the heart, the middle letter, of house

explanation.surface: A property document includes all the key details of a house sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deed' looks like a property title but means an action. 'what's essential to' gives U, the middle of 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Butcher's boy, by the way, taken in by venison supplier

indicators.note: taken in by says the next pieces are swallowed by the animal's letters

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the street's letters sit next to the boy's name

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Roy is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A butcher's lad, as it happens, has been cheated by the man who sells him deer meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the street beside the boy, and 'taken in by' puts the pair inside the animal. 'Butcher's' is the definition plus 's (has), not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to slaughter brutally, so a butcher is one who wrecks or kills, a synonym of destroyer.

clue.text: Back military leader to prepare for another war

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of military

explanation.surface: A call to support a general preparing for a new conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military leader' looks like a general but means the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply with weapons again, readying for a fresh conflict.

clue.text: Like aggressive bloke, swapping starter for Mexican dish

indicators.note: swapping starter means the first letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: macho describes a man who is aggressively masculine

explanation.surface: A tough guy trades his appetiser for a Mexican plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping starter' changes MACHO's first letter, M, for N. 'starter' here is a first letter, not an appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are tortilla chips topped with cheese, a Mexican snack.

clue.text: A diamond ring turns up in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a diamond is a gem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A diamond ring finally reappears after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses AGEMO to OMEGA. 'ring' gives O for its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end.

clue.text: Stand holding nearly every kind of bun

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first word's letters go round the next

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it, take it

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: every one means each one

explanation.surface: A display stand holds almost every variety of bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops a last letter and 'holding' signals the container. A TEACAKE is a British sweet bun, often toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light yeast bun containing dried fruit, usually eaten toasted.

clue.text: List originally missing an elusive person

indicators.note: originally missing means the original, first, letter is lost

parts.note: a ship that lists heels over, so a heel is a list

explanation.surface: A roll call that, from the start, lacks someone hard to pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a register but is a ship's tilt; 'originally missing' drops HEEL's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slippery as an eel is hard to catch, so eel is used for an elusive person.

clue.text: Deceive endlessly, at least more than once

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: two times is the least number that is more than once

explanation.surface: Someone is cheated over and over again, repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the final S from TWO TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time a partner is to be unfaithful to them in secret, a kind of deception.

clue.text: Discharge from office of speaker

indicators.note: of speaker means as the speaker would say it, so we want a word that sounds like the office

parts.note: an office is a room where work is done

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed from the office of the parliamentary Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker presides over the House of Commons, but here 'speaker' just means one saying the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: New Latin American capital recalled old Roman province

indicators.note: new means made new, so these letters are given a fresh order
recalled means called back, so this piece is read backwards

parts.note: A1, written with I for one, means excellent, a sense of capital

explanation.surface: A recent Latin American capital is said to have been named after an ancient Roman territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LATIN plus US into LUSITAN; 'recalled' turns AI (A1, capital in the sense 'excellent') into IA. 'Latin American capital' wants to be a city such as Lima.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusitania was the Roman province covering much of modern Portugal.
